allowed_write_paths: on each server: $STATE_DIR/last-reminder and pending (via that server's arch-maintenance.sh)

scripts.purpose: SKELETON - not implemented. Runs on this machine and invokes each host in REMOTE_SERVERS to execute that host's installed arch-maintenance.sh, so each server produces its own maintenance report and resets its own reminder state. Planned behavior: help and config-file options exit before any SSH; every host is attempted; a failed host is reported without hiding the others; a nonzero exit means at least one host failed. Open questions: whether this should also trigger the server's backup.sh, whether to pass a config file or other flags through to the remote script, whether non-interactive sudo is available on each server for the Timeshift check, and how per-host failures are aggregated.

arguments.name: -h|--help
arguments.description: Print usage and exit 0 before contacting any host.

arguments.name: -c|--config-file FILE
arguments.description: Load settings from FILE; takes precedence over USER_SCRIPTS_CONFIG and installed/legacy/repository lookup. A missing value exits 2.

arguments.name: --config-file=FILE
arguments.description: Equivalent to -c FILE; an empty value exits 2.

environment.name: USER_SCRIPTS_CONFIG
environment.description: Config file path used when no config-file option is given.

environment.name: XDG_CONFIG_HOME
environment.description: Base directory for the installed config lookup.

environment.name: REMOTE_SERVERS
environment.description: Array of user@host targets; an empty list makes this script a no-op that exits 0.

environment.name: REMOTE_INSTALL_DIR
environment.description: Directory on each server where arch-maintenance.sh is installed; planned command path.

environment.name: SSH_TIMEOUT
environment.description: Non-interactive ssh connect timeout in seconds.

write_paths: on each server: $STATE_DIR/last-reminder and pending (via that server's arch-maintenance.sh)

exit_codes.meaning: Help printed, or every configured host ran its maintenance successfully; an empty REMOTE_SERVERS is also success.
Config file unreadable, or at least one host could not be reached or its maintenance exited nonzero.
A config-file option was supplied without a non-empty value.
